note: Groups are the 127 g-percentiles of Gethin & Fisher-Post (2026), "Government Redistribution and Global Poverty Reduction", data version 2026-09-22: all individuals, with income split equally within couples (WID's 999j unit), ranked by pretax national income. Sizes and average incomes are theirs.

Amounts are in national currency at 2023 prices: Gethin-Fisher values (PPP USD of 2024) times defl (0.979333) times xppp_us (0.612659). Their ReadMe gives the PPP base year as 2023, but xppp_us matches WID's 2024 PPP, so we take the base to be 2024.
Check: total pretax income from Gethin-Fisher is 0.971 times WID's national income for 2023.

Lower thresholds come from WID's tptinc999j for 2023, made nominal and scaled by each group's ratio of Gethin-Fisher's to WID's average income (106 of 126 groups; 20 unscaled where that ratio was unavailable or outside 0.5-2). The bottom group's threshold is set to 0, since Gethin-Fisher's averages don't follow WID's negative incomes.
34 thresholds fell outside the averages of the groups on either side and were moved to the nearer one: p6p7 p7p8 p8p9 p9p10 p10p11 p11p12 p12p13 p13p14 p14p15 p15p16 p16p17 p17p18 ….

The current income tax rate by group (effectiveIncomeTaxShareOfIncome) is Gethin-Fisher's personal income tax (tax_dir_pit, their central estimate) over pretax income. Their lower and upper bounds aren't used.
5 groups have non-positive average income; their rate is set to 0.
Data quality Credible, from WID's data-quality score of 4 (out of 5) on the income thresholds: 4 or 5 is Credible, lower is Modeled.

paramIndividualIncomeTaxCalibratedBaseShareOfIncome (λ): each individual's pretax national income is scaled by λ before the current income tax schedule is applied, with λ chosen so the schedule reproduces Gethin-Fisher's total personal income tax (tax_dir_pit). λ absorbs allowances, deductions, credits, preferential rates, filing-unit effects and evasion, so it is not a measured taxable-income share.

The calibration applies the schedule to group excess curves built from the groups fixture: exact below each group's lower threshold, the midpoint of the upper and lower bounds within a group, and a Pareto tail in the top group (α = a/(a − m)). The model must build its curves the same way to reproduce the target. Target: income tax of 12.76% of pretax income; the schedule applied to all pretax income would raise 31.65%.
OECD Revenue Statistics: personal income tax (code 1100) was 11.22% of GDP in 2023 (central government 10.33%, local governments 0.90%).

Central government: the 2023 statutory schedule from the OECD Tax Database, "Personal income tax (PIT) - central government rates and thresholds" (SDMX dataflow OECD.CTP.TPS,DSD_TAX_PIT@DF_PIT_CENT), for a single person without dependents, applied to wage income. Thresholds are in national currency, nominal 2023. The OECD reports each bracket's upper limit; we store lower limits, starting at 0. 4 brackets, from 23% to a top rate of 43% above 50,000.

Sub-central governments levy a flat income tax; the OECD's representative rate, 3.33%, is added to every bracket. Rates range from 1.73% to 3.33% across localities; the OECD's representative rate is used, not a population-weighted average.
Combined central and sub-central schedule: 4 brackets, from 26.33% to a top rate of 46.33% above 50,000.
A basic tax credit of 1,880 is reported separately and is not part of the schedule; like allowances, it is absorbed by calibration.
Capital income (dividends, capital gains, interest) may be taxed under separate rules, e.g. at flat or preferential rates; the general model applies this schedule only.
